name: the MusicBrainz source ignores sa_pop_mb
why: The link previews are opt-in, off by default (org/iframe.org, answer 1): with the setting off a MusicBrainz page gets no stylesheet, no listener and no request.

name: the MusicBrainz cards ignore the Ctrl gate
why: They follow sa_dp_hover_without_ctrl, 'every preview' (answer 2): moving the pointer across a table full of links must neither pop up cards nor ask MusicBrainz.

name: any page under an entity is previewed, not just the bare one
why: The CAA/EAA icon column links /release/<id>/cover-art (artwork has its own preview); /edit and the tabs are not the entity either.

name: a link wrapping an image is previewed
why: An inline cover or thumbnail has its own hover preview (#mb-art-hover-preview); a card over it would be a second box.

name: a link in the Relationships column is previewed
why: The Relationships column has its own tooltip (#mb-rel-tooltip) on its cells.

name: a request nobody wants any more is still sent
why: The popup engine's rule: a hover that has moved on by the time its rate slot comes up makes no request (as _dpGet() on the foreign hosts); otherwise crossing a table queues one request per link.
grep: hover that moved on before its rate slot asks nothing; the gate

name: a release-group link's card does not pass its wanted() on
why: Phase 1's loader always wanted its pages (the release page's own sources still do); from a table link a moved-on hover must make no request.
grep: release-group link whose hover moved on

name: a failed answer is kept
why: Only a success is cached, everywhere in the script: a failure kept as done would never be asked again until the page reloads.
grep: a failure is shown, not kept

name: a repaint starts the card's request
why: Only a call with start may start a request: card() is called again by every repaint, and a repaint that started one would retry a failed request for ever (docs/claude/detail-pages.md).
grep: a failure is shown, not kept

name: the answers ignore sa_pop_mb_ttl_hours
why: MusicBrainz data changes daily; the setting says how long an answer is reused (answer 4), and a one-hour TTL must ask again for a two-hour-old answer.

name: the arrows stay in the first sub-table
why: On a multi-table page the column goes on in the next visible sub-table (the releases of a group split by status).

edits.replace:

name: the arrows mix kinds in a column
why: A row links a release, an artist, a label: the arrows step through ONE kind. Re-checked in WIP.3 with artist and label cards: on the host page every column holds one kind (its /cover-art anchors resolve to nothing), so the kind filter is still covered by the column match. Recorded so the overlap is known.

name: the card no longer rules out the Liner notes card
why: One box at a time: while the card shows, #mb-stat-tooltip shows no card of the same link (_OTHER_RICH_TIPS).

name: a tap on a MusicBrainz link follows it
why: The engine's tap rule, kept on MusicBrainz (decided 2026-10-07): a touch screen has no hover and no Ctrl, so a tap opens the window and its ↗ opens the page.
grep: a tap on a release link

name: the cache key leaves out the inc set
why: Two lookups of one recording with different inc sets (the card's, the window's credits) must not answer each other: the credits would come from the card's answer, which has no artist relations, and never be asked (_relFetchWs2()'s trap, org/iframe.org 'Risks').

name: the recording window always asks for the count
why: A lookup embeds at most 25 releases (Phase 0, R3): only a full list can mean more, so only then is the count worth a request.

name: a failed extra request is asked again by every repaint
why: pin() runs from repaints too; without the guard a failed credits lookup is asked again whenever anything else in the window answers, for ever.

name: ⟳ asks only the card's lookup again
why: ⟳ 'asks MusicBrainz again' for the whole window: the extras started from the lookup's own callback must get the ⟳ too.

edits.find: if (spec.pin && s && s.status === 'done') spec.pin(t, s.data, start && force, repaint);
edits.replace: if (spec.pin && s && s.status === 'done') spec.pin(t, s.data, false, repaint);

name: a full release list reads as exact
why: 25 is where the lookup stops, not the count (271 for Thunder Road): the card says '25+'.

name: relation groups lose their direction-aware names
why: A label owns some labels and is owned by another; 'Label ownership' twice says neither. _MB_POP_REL_LABELS names them as MusicBrainz's pages do.

name: relations are grouped by type only
why: Without the direction the label's parent lands among the labels it owns.

name: the artist card asks for its links
why: 75 URL relations were most of the artist lookup's 30 KB in Phase 0 (R1): the card leaves them to the window.

name: the label code is not padded
why: MusicBrainz shows a label code as 'LC' and five digits; the Web Service gives the bare integer (162).

name: the artist window counts one type only
why: Each primary type is its own browse (limit=1); the window shows all five as they arrive.

name: the setlist shows its [mbid|name] tokens raw
why: The Web Service gives the setlist in MusicBrainz's markup; a song shown as '[9893a23c-…|Born to Run]' is unreadable.

name: the line-up ignores the setlist's own joining words
why: 'Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band with Roy Bittan, …' is how the setlist bills them; commas alone lose the billing.

name: the event art is not loaded on pin
why: The poster comes from the Event Art Archive, its own host, only in the window (R4).

name: a place's events keep the browse's order
why: The event browse answers in no date order; the window promises 'by date'.

name: a series' items keep the lookup's order
why: The lookup lists the items by ordering key 1, 2, 10, 7, …; a series is read in its order.

name: a disc ID's page is taken for its kind
why: The site's page is /cdtoc/<id>, the Web Service's path /ws/2/discid/<id>: without the mapping a disc ID link previews nothing.

name: a code's page is built from its kind, not its path
why: ↗ and the Live page must open /cdtoc/<id>, the page the link named; /discid/<id> does not exist on the site.

name: a private collection's 401 gets no explanation
why: The Web Service shows public collections only; 'HTTP 401' alone reads like a fault of the script.
